images.prompt: Photorealistic macro photograph of a handcrafted miniature tabletop diorama. On a pale neutral tabletop, a frosted acrylic tile about the size of a playing card stands upright in a matte graphite stand, lit softly from within so its milky surface glows a clean acid-lime. This backlit tile is the scene's single lime element and the target colour. Directly in front of it lies a printed ivory card swatch of the same size, its patch a slightly duller, greener tone that almost matches. A small graphite loupe sits beside the card, and a sandblasted glass ruler lies parallel to the edge. The card's fibres and faint ink grain are visible up close. Everything is aligned and orderly, the only flaw being the small gap in tone between tile and print. Wide 16:9 landscape frame. The hero object sits slightly left of centre on the lower third, with the related objects extending to the right so the workflow reads left to right. Clean, generous negative space above. Shot as a real physical model, not a 3D render. Materials are limited and tactile: heavyweight ivory cotton paper and card with visible fibres, soft folds and slightly deckled edges; matte, bead-blasted graphite metal with fine machining lines, chamfered edges and tiny hex fasteners; frosted acrylic with milky edges and a soft internal glow; sandblasted frosted glass. Surfaces carry believable imperfections: fine dust, paper grain, hairline creases, light scuffs on metal. Every object has convincing miniature scale and weight and rests firmly on its surface. Colour palette is restrained and nearly monochrome: white #FFFFFF, warm ivory, pale neutral #F3F5F2, soft grey-green #DCE1DA, muted graphite #626A64 and deep graphite #191D1B. Acid lime #D0F344 appears only on the lime element named in the scene, as the single signal colour, with olive #718D0B on its shadowed sides. Nothing else is lime or saturated; no red, orange or blue accents. Lighting: one large soft key light from the upper left at about 45 degrees, like diffused north-window daylight, with a gentle white bounce fill from the right; soft grounded contact shadows fall to the lower right. Camera: 100mm macro lens at f/4, eye level with the tabletop, three-quarter view. The hero object is tack sharp and the background melts into smooth, creamy blur on a seamless pale neutral sweep. Mood: calm, precise, orderly and quietly premium, like high-end editorial product photography. Strictly no people, figures, faces, hands or silhouettes. No readable text, letters, numbers, clock digits, logos, signage or user-interface graphics anywhere. No holograms, floating screens, robots with faces, dense cable tangles, carnival or circus elements, cartoon or plastic CGI look, oversaturated colour, lens flare or heavy vignette.

Photorealistic macro photograph of a handcrafted miniature tabletop diorama, captured mid-disaster. The same graphite stand and glowing acid-lime acrylic tile remain at the back, but in front of them a long fan of printed swatch cards now spreads across the tabletop toward the viewer. Each card was copied from the previous one, and the tones drift in visible steps from a soft yellow-green to olive, then grey, then a flat muddy beige at the far end. The newest cards are still sliding off the fan and one is frozen mid-flip at the table edge. The loupe has been knocked over and rolled into the stack, and the glass ruler lies crooked beneath several cards. Fine ink dust and paper fibres hang above the fan, which traces straight back to the first card beside the tile. Wide 16:9 landscape frame, same layout and angle as the calm version of this scene. Nothing else is lime or saturated; no red, orange or blue accents. Photorealistic photograph of a vast handcrafted miniature landscape diorama. A shallow flooded basin stretches toward a misty horizon, its still grey water scattered with low islands made of stacked swatch cards, swollen, faded and warped into terraced mounds. The tones of the islands drift from pale green near the centre to dull beige at the edges. In the midground, the enormous graphite stand rises from the water like a ruined tower, and the frosted acrylic tile it once held lies cracked and clouded, half submerged at its base. Tide lines of ink stain the card islands. On the nearest island, a slim graphite tripod calibration rig on long thin legs holds an acid-lime reference lens over the first swatch, a fine lime probe pressing its patch back toward the right tone. Wide 16:9 panoramic frame. The main ruin anchors the left or centre foreground, terrain rolls back to a distant horizon on the upper third, and the lime recovery rig sits in the right midground. Surfaces carry believable imperfections: fine dust, paper grain, hairline creases, light scuffs on metal. Every object has convincing miniature scale and weight and rests firmly on its surface. Nothing else is lime or saturated; no red, orange or blue accents.
